name: Associated Press on AI: newsroom tools, local news projects and coverage
title: Associated Press on AI: newsroom tools, local news projects and coverage
answer: This is the website of The Associated Press, the American wire service, and its AI material includes AP's own account of how it uses artificial intelligence in news production alongside reporting on AI in campaigns, games and public trust. The most useful part for media readers is AP's description of deployed tools: video shotlisting with editorial review, Merlin search that recognises elements in photos and videos without metadata, and English to Spanish translation with a human in the loop.

sections.body: ap.org is the website of The Associated Press, the American wire service. The AI-relevant material read across 60 pages includes AP's artificial intelligence solutions page, which describes how AP deploys AI in news gathering, production and distribution, plus AP news articles on AI in political campaigns, video games, seniors' education and public trust in AI election information. It also refers to the AP Stylebook's artificial intelligence chapter, AP's Local News AI initiative and its 2022 report on AI readiness in local news. The dated material runs from a 2022 investigative series and report to 2023 projects and 2024 articles.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: AP's artificial intelligence solutions page sets out how the wire service deploys AI in news gathering, production and distribution. It uses AI-driven tools to analyse video and build shotlists, with every generated description reviewed and edited by editorial staff before publication, and says shotlists are meant to help customers find shots inside a clip rather than be republished. Merlin, its AI-powered search, recognises elements within photos and videos without relying on descriptions or metadata. AP has rolled out generative AI translation from English to Spanish with a human in the loop, and uses AI to generate concise summaries. It works with AppliedXL on analysing federal registry data for local news tips and with ShortTok on content discovery and video curation. Under its Local News AI initiative, funded by the John S. and James L. Knight Foundation, AP developed five projects in 2023: automated public safety incident writing at the Brainerd Dispatch in Minnesota, Spanish-language weather alerts at El Vocero de Puerto Rico, transcription and summarisation at KSAT-TV in San Antonio, news tip sorting at WFMZ-TV in Allentown, and expanded meeting transcripts with summarisation and reporter alerts at Michigan Radio's WUOM-FM. A Patrick J. McGovern Foundation grant supports training, including tip sheets, LocalizeIt guides and the AP Stylebook's AI chapter. AP's news coverage examined deepfakes in a Shreveport mayoral race, generative non-player characters in games, AI classes for seniors and public distrust of AI election information.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: AP reports that about two thirds of U.S. adults are not very or not at all confident that AI-powered chatbots or search results provide reliable and factual information, from a survey with NORC and USAFacts. It says more than a third of states have passed laws regulating AI in politics, according to Public Citizen. A Game Developers Conference report found nearly half of developers surveyed said generative AI tools are used in their workplace, 31% said they personally use them, 37% at indie studios did, and roughly four out of five worried about ethical use. An AARP report said Americans over 60 lose $28.3 billion annually to financial extortion schemes. AP developed five AI projects in 2023, and its Tracked series brought together more than 40 AP journalists.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in media, this is an operating newsroom describing systems it has actually deployed rather than a vendor describing a roadmap. The shotlisting, Merlin search, translation and summarisation work, and the five local newsroom projects, give concrete examples of where AI sits in a production chain and where human review is retained. The Stylebook chapter, tip sheets and LocalizeIt guides offer guidance a newsroom can adopt, while the reporting on deepfakes, election misinformation and public distrust supplies context on the risks that accompany adoption.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Media

sections.body: The solutions page is AP describing and promoting its own products and partnerships, so it is not neutral. The news articles are journalism about other organisations' use of AI rather than accounts of AP's own systems. There is no pricing, no detail on the models behind the tools and no evaluation of accuracy. The AI-specific material is dated 2022 to 2024, and one survey page is only partly captured in the record read.
